title: P6 steps 2 and 8b: the exact numeric core of the VectorDB family (rholang/src/rust/interpreter/tensor) and its Rocq model Similarity.v, and the VectorDB discipline of one collection (the driver of disciplines/vectordb.rs and the similarity paths of the join engine) and its Rocq model VectorDbDiscipline.v, and its TLA+ model VectorDb.tla, the replies of rho:lang:vector (tensor/ops.rs) and their Rocq model VectorOps.v, and the ChromaDB mirror of a VectorDB space (the capture, the journal, the writer, the reconciler and the recorded process ann) and its TLA+ model ChromaMirror.tla.
design: P6 design v3 (.reified-rspaces-work/p6/design-v3.md), sections 4.1, 4.3 to 4.6 and 5. The headline ids are the ids of the P6 phase of formal/reified-rspaces-invariant-map.json.
code_base: The items are in the P6 commits of steps 2, 6, 7a to 7c and 8b of this repository. The line numbers are informative. The checker finds each item by its scope and name.

S1.name: cosine_squared_form_iff
S1.statement: In every ordered commutative ring, the real numbers included: for s = |q|·|e| > 0, t·s ≤ q·e (cos ≥ t) holds exactly when cosine_within(q·e, t, s·s), the decision of within, which uses no root.

S2.name: cosine_order_squared_form
S2.statement: With s_i·s_i = |q|²·|e_i|², the real order cos_1 ≤ cos_2 holds exactly when cosine_le, the order of better, which cross-multiplies the squares by the norms of the other record.

S3.name: euclidean_radius_squared_form
S3.statement: For a distance d ≥ 0, d ≤ r holds exactly when euclidean_within(d², r): r ≥ 0 and d² ≤ r².

S4.name: threshold_monotone
S4.statement: A lower threshold admits every record that a higher threshold admits, under cosine, dot and jaccard.

S5.name: radius_monotone
S5.statement: A larger radius admits every record that a smaller radius admits, under euclidean, manhattan and hamming.

S6.name: dot_laws
S6.statement: The dot product is symmetric, and its exact sum does not depend on the order of the coordinates.

S7.name: distance_laws
S7.statement: dist2 is non-negative, symmetric and zero exactly on equal vectors; manhattan is non-negative, symmetric and satisfies the triangle inequality.

S9.name: cosine_bounds
S9.statement: Every record passes the cosine threshold −1, and no record passes a threshold above 1.

S10.name: score_orders_total
S10.statement: The order of each of the six metrics is a total preorder on its scores: cosine over positive record norms, dot and the distances by their values, jaccard over positive unions.

S11.name: squared_forms_embed
S11.statement: An embedding of ordered rings keeps the decisions of S1 to S3, so the decisions in the rationals are the decisions in the real numbers.

S12.name: binary_laws
S12.statement: Hamming is a metric on binary vectors, the jaccard counts satisfy inter ≤ union and are symmetric, and the union is empty only when neither vector sets a position.

S13.name: selection_total_order
S13.statement: The selection order (the better score, then the lower DR-75 rank) is irreflexive, transitive and total on distinct ranks.

S14.name: topk_deterministic
S14.statement: Two sorted arrangements of one multiset of candidates are equal, so their first k candidates are equal.

S15.name: list_selection_deterministic
S15.statement: List mode, the first k eligible candidates in the selection order, depends only on the multiset of records, and the insertion sort computes it.

S16.name: kappa_dropped_not_unique
S16.statement: Negative control: by score alone, two equal-score records have two sorted arrangements with different first records.

S17.name: Qc_ordered_ring
S17.statement: The canonical rationals satisfy every hypothesis of the ordered ring of Part 1.

S18.name: similarity_headlines_Qc
S18.statement: S1, S2, S3, S8 and S9 hold in the canonical rationals.

S19.name: squared_forms_embed_Z_Qc
S19.statement: S11 holds for the embedding of the integers into the rationals.

S20.name: selection_Qc
S20.statement: S13 and S14 hold for rational scores.

S21.name: vdb_join_removal_exposes_nothing
S21.statement: A removal keeps the order of each similarity window, so a greedy search of single-mode binds that fails before a removal fails after it. The search of one bind is the selection of the driver (design v3 4.6).

S22.name: vdb_no_pending_match
S22.statement: A transaction that ends leaves no parked waiter without a guard that can fire, in single mode and in list mode (LM-b, decision 66).

S23.name: vdb_list_needs_cascade
S23.statement: Negative result, computed: without LIST-CASCADE a receive ends with a parked list waiter that can fire (the counterexample CE-2 of the arbitration).

S24.name: vdb_txn_bounded
S24.statement: For a cap above 0, a transaction makes at most cap fires, and each loop of RECEIVE-VDB, OFFER-VDB and the tail ends within the fuel that the plans compute (I-21, decision 49).

S25.name: vdb_no_record_lost
S25.statement: Rule E (decision 45): a record of the pre-state is in the post-state of a transaction that ends, or a fire of a waiter that does not peek spent it.

S26.name: replay_reproduces_play_run
S26.statement: Replay stages the operations of play, pairs each recorded COMM once, and reproduces the run of play: its observer calls, its effects and its status (H23, decision 36). The VectorDB plans stage through the substrate, so their transactions replay this way.

W1.name: QuiescentNoPendingMatch
W1.statement: With no re-issued operation and no settle job outstanding, no parked waiter can fire on the records, for every schedule of the bounded configurations, with settle jobs and re-issues at the round cap (LM-b).

W2.name: ListAtomic
W2.statement: A list fire of a waiter that does not peek spends each member of its list that is not persistent, in the transaction of the fire (K_retire and K_lift).

W3.name: PeekConservation
W3.statement: Every record that was stored is stored, spent by a fire of a waiter that does not peek, or pending in an outstanding settle job (Rule E, decisions 30 and 45).

W4.name: CascadeTerminates
W4.statement: Each step of each tail lowers the measure 2 * (Cap - fired) + |owed| or stops the transaction, and no transaction runs out of its fuel (decision 49, I-21).

S27.name: vector_replies_exact
S27.statement: The reply of add, scale and dot has the widest kind of the inputs. It is the exact value for the integer and the rational kinds, and one rounding of the exact value for the float kind: dot rounds its exact sum once (decisions 54 and 66).

S28.name: root_midpoint_nearest
S28.statement: When the squares of the midpoints between a representable reply r and its neighbours bound x = s * s with s >= 0, no representable value is nearer to s than r: the check of the correctly rounded roots of norm and distance.

W5.name: ConsensusIndependentOfMirror
W5.statement: The post-state of each deploy is a function of its pre-state and its recorded answer only: no mirror write runs in a transaction (design v3 4.9).

W6.name: AdvisoryRecorded
W6.statement: Replay uses the recorded answer of ann and never asks its own mirror (decision 57).

W7.name: EqualHostWork
W7.statement: Play and replay make the same checks of an ann call, so they reserve the same host work for them (decision 67).

W8.name: PublishOnlyOnSuccess
W8.statement: Every published write comes from a deploy whose final result has no errors, and the clear at the start of a root evaluation drops the journal of an exploratory evaluation (M1, decision 66).

W9.name: NetWritesExact
W9.statement: A published batch upserts exactly the records that its deploy added and deletes exactly the records that it removed, so a Rule E pair writes nothing.

W10.name: PublishNeverWaits
W10.statement: A publication never waits for the writer: a full queue marks the collection dirty (decision 58).

W11.name: ReconciledEqualsFinalizedView
W11.statement: After a reconciler pass that finishes, the mirror holds the finalized view on every registered channel (decision 66).

W12.name: WatermarkHonest
W12.statement: The watermark of a collection never passes the block of the last reconciler pass that finished.

items.name: new
items.role: The query of a receive: ‖q‖² for cosine (a zero query has no direction and is refused), and the bits for hamming and jaccard.

items.name: add
items.role: The exact sum of dyadic terms with the least exponent as its unit: no rounding, so the sum does not depend on the order of the terms.

items.name: dot
items.role: The exact dot product, by DYADIC-SUM or by reduced rationals.

items.name: distance2
items.role: The exact squared euclidean distance.

items.name: manhattan
items.role: The exact manhattan distance.

items.name: bits
items.role: The bits of a binary vector, or None when an element is not 0 or 1 (decision 66).

items.name: hamming
items.role: The hamming distance of two bit vectors.

items.name: jaccard
items.role: The intersection and the union of two bit vectors, or None for an empty union.

items.name: score
items.role: The exact score of a record for a query, or None when it is undefined.

items.name: better
items.role: The exact order of two scores of one query: COSINE-BETTER, the values, and the cross-multiplied jaccard ratios.

items.name: within
items.role: The exact bound decisions: the squared forms of cosine and euclidean, and the other thresholds and radii.

items.name: Candidate
items.role: A candidate of a selection: its score and its rank in the canonical order of DR-75.

items.name: selection_order
items.role: The selection order: the better score, then the lower rank (decisions 41 and 60).

items.name: rank
items.role: The metered heap sort of the candidates in the selection order.

items.name: Exact
items.role: The exact numbers of the core: reduced rationals (num_rational::BigRational), which Qc models; the property test checks the ordered ring laws that Part 5 discharges for Qc.

items.name: number_of
items.role: The exact value of every number kind: a dyadic number or a reduced rational, so every decision is a decision of the rationals.

items.name: vector_of
items.role: The exact vector of a list of numbers, with its dimension checked.

items.name: delivered
items.role: The delivered value RN_53 of an exact score.
items.unmodeled: Rocq has no IEEE-754 model (plan, formal verification). The Rust oracle tests against IEEE division and square root, the Sage leg (MPFR) and the Python receipt check it against test-vectors/numeric-reference-v1.json.

items.name: round_to_f64
items.role: RN_53 of a rational.
items.unmodeled: Rocq has no IEEE-754 model. The IEEE quotient and identity oracles, the Sage leg and the Python receipt check it.

items.name: sqrt_to_f64
items.role: RN_53 of the square root of a rational. S28 states what the midpoint check of its reply proves: no f64 is nearer to the root. The IEEE quotient and square root oracles, the Sage leg and the Python receipt check the encoding.

items.name: Element
items.role: The element in flight of an offer: a datum, a second send of Rule E or a lifted record, with the identity of its produce and its persistence.

items.name: eligible
items.role: The eligibility of a record for a query (its score, the bound and the ids), which orders the eligible records by the selection order of tensor/exact.rs.

items.name: list_selection
items.role: List mode: the first k eligible records in the selection order, bound as one list when the pattern binds it.

items.name: list_offer
items.role: The list of a list waiter with the element in flight at its place: the waiter fires when the list holds the element.

items.name: retire_members
items.role: K_retire: the other non-persistent members of a list that a fire of a waiter without a peek spends.

items.name: offer_vdb
items.role: OFFER-VDB: the element fires the first waiter that it fires, or it is stored, and a fire that does not spend it offers it again (decision 30).

items.name: first_offer_target
items.role: The first parked waiter in DR-75 order that the element fires.

items.name: receive_plan
items.role: RECEIVE-VDB: the receive fires on its selection or parks, a persistent receive fires again, and a peek owes its removed members as second sends (Rule E). Then the tail runs.

items.name: receive_selection
items.role: The selection of a receive: plain, single mode or list mode.

items.name: run_tail
items.role: The tail: the owed second sends first, then LIST-CASCADE, with the round cap checked before each fire.

items.name: first_cascade_target
items.role: The first parked list waiter in DR-75 order whose list is acceptable now.

items.name: lift_and_reoffer
items.role: LIFT-AND-REOFFER of a list target: the first member is lifted (K_lift), the waiter fires, the other members retire without a peek, and a peek owes the lifted member again.

items.name: after_fire
items.role: The step after one fire: Done when the incoming side is spent, a divergent-pair stop when its partner stays, a round-cap stop at FIRE_ROUND_CAP, else Continue.

items.name: window
items.role: The window of a bind: for JoinWindow::Similarity, the eligible records of the query of the bind in its selection order.

items.name: search
items.role: The greedy search of the engine over the positions of a join, each over its own window.

items.name: similarity_bind
items.role: The first record of the selection order of a bind that its pattern binds, without the records that earlier binds claimed.

items.name: finish_tail
items.role: The tail of a plan: an element of the operation that stopped at the round cap stops the transaction when work is owed, and otherwise only re-issues; after a divergent pair, or when the element settled, the tail runs.

items.name: conclude
items.role: The re-issue at the end of a plan: one settle job with the pending second sends and the resume operation, or the re-issue of the operation alone.

items.name: classify
items.role: A settle job with a cascade state always runs in the join engine.

items.name: commit
items.role: COMMIT of the engine: a stop with owed work re-issues one settle job with the pending sends and the resume operation, and otherwise the resume operation.

items.name: drain_and_cascade
items.role: DRAIN-AND-CASCADE of a settle job: the pending second sends first, then the cascade, with the round cap checked before each fire.

items.name: Kind
items.role: The kinds of a number of rho:lang:vector, ordered by width: Integer, Rational, Float.

items.name: kind_of
items.role: The kind of a numeric Par: GInt, GBigInt and GBool are integers, GBigRat and GFixedPoint are rationals, GDouble and GFloat32 are floats.

items.name: vector_operand
items.role: A vector operand and the widest kind of its elements (Integer for no element).

items.name: add
items.role: a + b, exact, encoded in the wider kind of the two vectors.

items.name: scale
items.role: s * v, exact, encoded in the wider kind of the vector and the factor.

items.name: evaluate
items.role: The value of a call of rho:lang:vector: add, scale and dot in the widest kind, norm and distance as the correctly rounded root of an exact square.

items.name: number_par
items.role: The exact value encoded in a kind: GInt or GBigInt, GBigRat, or one rounding to a GDouble.

items.name: vector
items.role: The process rho:lang:vector: it replies the value of evaluate on the return channel.

items.name: writes
items.role: The net writes of one committed transaction: the first and the last event of each record id decide an upsert, a delete or nothing.

items.name: record
items.role: Appends the net writes of a transaction to the journal of the evaluation: the last write of each record id wins.

items.name: take
items.role: Removes the writes of the journal as one batch for each collection.

items.name: clear
items.role: Drops the writes of the journal.

items.name: run_op
items.role: A space job: its transaction records the net writes in the journal and never writes the mirror.

items.name: settle_mirror_journal
items.role: M1: a final result without errors publishes the journal, and any other result drops it.

items.name: begin_evaluation_scope
items.role: The start of a root evaluation drops a journal that no result settled.

items.name: publish
items.role: Hands the batches to the bounded queue with try_send and never waits: a refused batch marks its collection dirty.

items.name: spawn_with
items.role: The writer task: it applies the batches in order with bounded attempts, and a batch that still fails marks its collection dirty.

items.name: apply
items.role: The writes of one batch in order: the collection, the registration of its channels, the upserts, the deletes.

items.name: reconcile
items.role: One reconciler pass for a finalized block: it prepares the dirty collections and repairs each collection below the block or dirty.

items.name: prepare_dirty
items.role: Makes a dirty collection and registers the channels of its unapplied batches.

items.name: remark
items.role: Marks a dirty collection dirty again after a pass that did not repair it.

items.name: repair
items.role: Repairs the registered channels of a collection to the finalized state, then sets the watermark to the larger of the block and the old watermark.

items.name: channel_repair
items.role: The orphans and the missing records of one registered channel at the finalized state.

items.name: ann
items.role: The process rho:vectordb:ann: the checks of consensus state in play and in replay, then the recorded reply in replay or the answer of the services in play.

items.name: ann_request
items.role: The checks of an ann call (decision 67): a mirrored VectorDB space, a query of its dimensions, and k in [1, capacity].

items.name: ann_answer
items.role: The answer of the services in play: the neighbours and the watermark of the mirror, which the dispatcher records.

items.name: produce_recorded
items.role: Produces the output of a recorded process and keeps it on a failed produce, so the dispatcher records it.
